per_question.question: Are there quantity limits on prescription drugs under NC Medicaid, and when is prior authorization required for pharmacy claims?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes. Under **NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 9**, pharmacy claims can be subject to **quantity limitations**, and **prior authorization** is required for drugs or uses that NC Medicaid identifies as needing prior approval. The current policy document I relied on is **Policy 9, effective July 15, 2024**, and I checked for amendments to confirm it is current. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

## Quantity limits

Policy 9 expressly refers to **“quantity limitations of episodic drugs”** and to **“drugs that are prescribed in limited quantities.”** It places those rules in the dispensing/max supply section rather than the prior-approval drug list. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

Specifically, **Section 5.4.3, “Quantity and Episodic Drugs,”** addresses:
- evaluating whether quantity limitations apply to episodic drugs,
- prior authorization criteria and requirements, and
- actions to minimize dispensing fees for drugs prescribed in limited quantities. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

So the answer is **yes**: NC Medicaid does have quantity-limit rules for some outpatient pharmacy claims.

What I **could verify from the policy text** is the existence of those limits and that some limited-quantity situations tie into PA criteria. What I **could not verify from the retrieved text here** is a single universal numeric cap that applies to all prescription drugs; the policy text I retrieved points to category-specific quantity limits rather than one across-the-board limit. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

## When prior authorization is required

Under **Policy 9**, prior authorization is required when the drug or use falls into NC Medicaid’s **pharmacy prior approval criteria**.

### 1) Drugs on the pharmacy prior approval list
Policy 9 includes a section titled **“Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria”** listing categories of drugs that require prior approval criteria, including examples such as:
- GLP-1 receptor agonists and combinations
- growth hormones
- hepatitis C medications
- opioid analgesics
- PCSK9 inhibitors
- triptans
- Botox/Myobloc/Dysport/Xeomin
- CGM systems and related supplies
- and many other listed categories. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

That list appears in **Attachment K: Pharmacy Prior Approval Criteria** / **Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria**. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

### 2) Exception requests to FDA/NC Medicaid drug criteria
If a requested drug does not fit standard FDA-approved or NC Medicaid drug criteria, **Section 3.2.3** shows that an exception request requires documentation such as:
- health record information showing medical necessity,
- explanation of what other drugs were tried or why they cannot be tried,
- explanation from the prescriber why FDA-approved guidelines/evidence-based standards or NC Medicaid drug criteria are insufficient, and
- supporting compendia or peer-reviewed medical literature. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

This indicates PA is also required when the prescriber is seeking coverage outside ordinary criteria and must justify an exception.

### 3) New products/indications/dosing changes
Policy 9’s **Section 5.1, “Prior Authorization,”** states PA applies to:
- new variations of products already in the marketplace,
- new indications for products already in the marketplace,
- changes in indications for products, and
- changes in dosing for products already in the marketplace. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

## Important distinction: quantity limits vs. PA

These are related, but they are **not the same rule**:

- **Quantity limits** govern how much of certain drugs can be dispensed or whether limited-quantity dispensing rules apply. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)
- **Prior authorization** governs whether NC Medicaid must approve the drug, indication, dosing change, or exception request before the claim will pay. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

A claim may therefore:
- be subject to a **quantity limit**,
- require **prior authorization**,
- or involve **both**.

## EPSDT point

For beneficiaries under 21, **EPSDT does not eliminate a prior approval requirement** when the service or drug otherwise requires prior approval. [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

- **Yes, NC Medicaid imposes quantity limits on some prescription drugs.**
- **Prior authorization is required when the drug/category appears in Policy 9’s pharmacy prior approval criteria, when the claim seeks an exception to standard FDA/NC Medicaid drug criteria, and for certain new products, indications, indication changes, or dosing changes.** [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

If you want, I can next pull out the **specific quantity-limit/max-supply sections** or help identify whether a **particular drug** requires prior authorization under Policy 9.
